dossier.summary: Meridian Facility Group provides mechanical, electrical and janitorial maintenance for office campuses and hospitals in the Carolinas. Its site promises 24-hour response for contract clients and lists about 180 technicians.
dossier.why_now: Won a multi-site hospital maintenance contract in September, according to a news post on its site.

data.intro: Meridian's new multi-site hospital contract comes with a 24-hour response promise, and these five questions are the ones that decide whether about 180 technicians can keep it.

lines.ahead: Live dispatch across sites usually shows up as faster response on contract calls, and the lead holds when every site runs the same board.
lines.level: Most facilities services firms set the day in advance, and the next step is usually a board that moves work between sites during the day.
lines.behind: Closing this gap usually starts with one schedule every site and every technician can see, before any automatic routing.

lines.ahead: More jobs per technician on a campus usually means tight walking routes and stocked carts, and it holds when the morning starts on time.
lines.level: Most facilities services firms land in the middle on jobs per day, and the next step usually comes from grouping work by building.
lines.behind: Closing this gap usually means looking at travel between sites and trips to the store room, since those hours never show on a ticket.

lines.ahead: Invoicing within a day usually means the technician closes the work order on site, and keeping it there is what keeps billing disputes rare.
lines.level: Most facilities services firms bill within the week, and the next step is usually closing the work order before the technician leaves the floor.
lines.behind: Closing this gap usually means moving the close-out from the office to the site, so the invoice leaves while the client still remembers the visit.

lines.ahead: A high first-visit completion rate usually comes from asset history and stocked parts, and it holds while dispatch matches the trade to the call.
lines.level: Most facilities services firms complete most jobs on the first visit, and the next step is usually better asset notes before the technician arrives.
lines.behind: Closing this gap usually starts with what a technician knows before arriving: the asset history, the last visit and the parts it usually needs.

lines.ahead: Live arrival updates usually mean fewer calls from site managers, and the lead holds as long as the schedule behind them stays accurate.
lines.level: Most facilities services firms message the site contact by hand, and the next step is usually an automatic text tied to the schedule.
lines.behind: Closing this gap usually starts with an automatic message to the site contact on the morning of the visit, which also cuts calls into the desk.
